Lemma
[Index one yields a simple eigenpair]

↗ lem:signature-and-eigenvalue-signs ↗ def:simple-eigenpair

In the preceding setting, if $B$ has index $1$, then $A$ has one negative eigenvalue $\lambda $, counted with multiplicity; its eigenspace is a line, and any nonzero vector $u$ in it makes $(A,u,\lambda )$ a simple eigenpair.

Proof

↗ lem:signature-and-eigenvalue-signs ↗ def:simple-eigenpair \sketch The preceding lemma gives exactly one negative eigenvalue in an eigenbasis. Hence its eigenspace has dimension one and equals the span of any nonzero eigenvector in it.

□
